GreenVale Farmers Cooperative
MEETING MINUTES – 2024 SERIES

Minutes of the 1st General Meeting of the GreenVale Farmers Cooperative Society (GVFC)
Held at the Cooperative Hall, Gwagwa Village, Kaduna State
Date: Saturday, 13 April 2024
Time: 10:00 a.m. – 1:15 p.m. (WAT)

In attendance:
1. Alhaji Musa Ibrahim – Chairman (presiding)
2. Mrs. Grace Audu – Secretary
3. Mr. Peter Danjuma – Treasurer
4. Hajiya Aisha Bello – Member
5. Mr. Samuel Okonkwo – Member
6. Mr. Tunde Adeyemi – Member
7. Mrs. Fatima Sani – Member
8. Mr. Emmanuel Nwachukwu – Member
9. Mr. John Bature – Member
10. Mrs. Maryam Abubakar – Member
11. Mr. Ibrahim Musa – Member
12. Mrs. Ruth Garba – Member

Also present: Mr. Danladi Yakubu (Field Officer, Kaduna Agricultural Development Project) as guest.

1. Opening
The Chairman welcomed all members and guests. He thanked everyone for attending the first general meeting of the year. He reminded members that the cooperative was established in 2019 and now has 47 registered members. The meeting was declared open at 10:05 a.m.

2. Reading and Adoption of the Constitution
The Chairman read out key sections of the cooperative constitution. He reminded members that the constitution is the governing document of the cooperative. According to the cooperative constitution, GreenVale Farmers Cooperative headquarters_location is Gwagwa Village, Kaduna State. Record status: current. This was noted as the official address for all correspondence and records. The Chairman called for a motion to adopt the constitution as read.

Motion: That the constitution be adopted as the governing document of the cooperative.
Proposed by: Mr. Samuel Okonkwo
Seconded by: Mrs. Fatima Sani
Vote: Unanimous

3. Report of the Treasurer
Mr. Peter Danjuma presented the financial report for the period January – March 2024.

Income:
- Members’ contributions (47 members × NGN 2,000 monthly) – NGN 282,000
- Sale of maize from last season – NGN 150,000
- Registration fees (new members) – NGN 20,000
- Total income – NGN 452,000

Expenditure:
- Purchase of fertilizer – NGN 180,000
- Fuel for tractor – NGN 45,000
- Repairs to storage shed – NGN 30,000
- Stationery and records – NGN 8,500
- Transport for produce delivery – NGN 22,000
- Total expenditure – NGN 285,500

Balance as at 31 March 2024: NGN 166,500

The Treasurer noted that the balance was lower than expected due to the cost of fertilizer. He proposed that the cooperative consider bulk purchasing of inputs to reduce costs. Members discussed this and agreed to explore the option before the next planting season.

4. Report of the Field Officer
Mr. Danladi Yakubu gave a brief talk on the upcoming farming season. He advised members to prepare their land early and to use improved seed varieties. He mentioned that the Kaduna State Government had a programme for subsidised seedlings for registered cooperatives. He asked the cooperative to submit a letter of interest to the Ministry of Agriculture before 30 April 2024.

The Chairman thanked Mr. Yakubu for his visit. He asked the Secretary to prepare the letter of interest.

5. Election of Additional Executive Members
The Chairman announced that the cooperative needed to elect two additional members to the executive committee. The positions were:
- Assistant Secretary
- Welfare Officer

Nominations were received as follows:
For Assistant Secretary:
- Mrs. Ruth Garba (nominated by Mr. John Bature, seconded by Mrs. Maryam Abubakar)
- Mr. Emmanuel Nwachukwu (nominated by Mr. Tunde Adeyemi, seconded by Hajiya Aisha Bello)

For Welfare Officer:
- Mrs. Maryam Abubakar (nominated by Mrs. Fatima Sani, seconded by Mr. Samuel Okonkwo)
- Mr. Ibrahim Musa (nominated by Mr. John Bature, seconded by Mrs. Ruth Garba)
Apologies: Mr. Danjuma Bello, Mrs. Ruth Garba, Mr. Peter Adamu, Mrs. Mary Dauda, Mr. Stephen Yakubu

1. Opening
The meeting was called to order at 10:05 a.m. by the Chairman, Alhaji Suleiman Garba. He welcomed members and noted that this meeting was important for planning the upcoming planting season. He asked the Secretary to read the minutes of the previous meeting held on 14 April 2024.

2. Reading and Adoption of Previous Minutes
The minutes of the meeting of 14 April 2024 were read by the Secretary, Mrs. Hauwa Bello. Members were asked to raise any corrections.

Mr. John Bature said that the amount recorded for the sale of maize should be NGN 150,000 and not NGN 150,00 as written in the draft. The Secretary confirmed that the figure was correct and that the error was in the typing. The minutes were then adopted as a true record of the meeting. The adoption was proposed by Mr. Emmanuel Nwachukwu and seconded by Mrs. Lami Dogo.

Matters Arising:
- Members were reminded that the letter of interest for the Kaduna State Government seedlings programme was submitted to the Ministry of Agriculture on 29 April 2024. The Secretary confirmed that the letter was delivered by hand and a copy was retained in the cooperative's file.
- The Chairman reported that the Ministry had acknowledged receipt and that the cooperative should expect a response within two to three weeks.

3. Report of the Secretary
Mrs. Hauwa Bello gave a report on administrative matters since the last meeting.

a. Membership Status
The cooperative now has 47 registered members. Three new members were registered in April:
- Mr. Bitrus Tanko (sponsored by Mr. Danjuma Saleh)
- Mrs. Rebecca Dogo (sponsored by Mrs. Lami Dogo)
- Mr. Timothy Danladi (sponsored by Mr. Iliya Markus)

b. Communication and Contact List
The Secretary informed members that the cooperative email list had been updated. She said that all members who had provided email addresses were now included. The cooperative email list records Hauwa Bello email_address as hauwa.bello@gvfc.org. Record status: current. This is the current address for official correspondence from the cooperative. She asked members to note that any changes to their contact details should be given to her in writing so that the list could be kept up to date.

c. Records and Filing
The Secretary reported that the cooperative's records, including minutes, financial statements, and correspondence with the Ministry, were now kept in a filing cabinet donated by the Chairman. She asked members to avoid taking files home without signing the movement register.

4. Report of the Treasurer
Mr. Peter Danjuma presented the financial report for the period 1 April 2024 to 11 May 2024.

Income:
- Members’ contributions (April) – NGN 94,000
- Members’ contributions (May, partial) – NGN 66,000
- Sale of empty bags – NGN 3,500
- Total income – NGN 163,500

Expenditure:
- Fuel for tractor (ploughing) – NGN 38,000
- Purchase of improved seed (maize) – NGN 52,000
- Repairs to water pump – NGN 12,500
- Transport for seedlings application – NGN 4,000
- Stationery – NGN 2,200
- Total expenditure – NGN 108,700

Balance as at 11 May 2024: NGN 54,800

The Treasurer noted that the balance was lower than expected because members had not yet paid their full May contributions. He reminded members that contributions were due by the 5th of each month. Members who had not paid were asked to do so before the end of May.

The Chairman thanked the Treasurer for the report.

5. Report of the Field Officer
Mr. Danladi Yakubu gave an update on the seedlings programme. He said that the cooperative's application had been received and that the Ministry would be distributing improved maize and soybean seeds to registered cooperatives in the first week of June. The cooperative had been allocated:
- 50 kg of improved maize seed (SAMAZ 15)
- 25 kg of soybean seed
Income:
- Members’ contributions (May, balance) – NGN 41,000
- Sale of empty bags – NGN 1,200
- Total income – NGN 42,200

Expenditure:
- Fuel for tractor – NGN 15,000
- Purchase of 10 kg of maize seed (for demonstration plot) – NGN 6,000
- Transport for seed application follow-up – NGN 3,500
- Total expenditure – NGN 24,500

Balance as at 24 May 2024: NGN 17,700

The Treasurer noted that the cooperative’s total balance, including the amount reported at the previous meeting, stood at NGN 72,500. He said that this amount would be used to purchase inputs for the wet season farming. Members asked whether the cooperative could afford to buy a sprayer. The Treasurer said that a sprayer would cost about NGN 35,000, and that the cooperative could not currently afford it. The Chairman said that the matter would be considered at the next meeting.

5. Report of the Chairman
The Chairman reported on his visit to the Ministry of Agriculture office in Kaduna. He said that the cooperative had been registered with the Ministry since 2019, but that the Ministry had asked all cooperatives to update their registration details. The Chairman said that the cooperative needed to submit the following documents before the end of June:
- Updated list of members and their contact details
- Copy of the cooperative’s constitution
- Copy of the last audited financial statement
- Letter from the village head confirming the cooperative’s address

The Chairman asked the Secretary to prepare the documents and to liaise with the Ministry. Members agreed that the cooperative should pay the registration renewal fee of NGN 5,000.

6. Date of the Next Annual General Meeting
The Chairman raised the matter of the Annual General Meeting (AGM). He said that the cooperative’s constitution required that an AGM be held once a year. The last AGM was held in December 2023. Members discussed possible dates for the next AGM. Some members suggested holding it in October, before the harvest season. Others suggested December, after the harvest, when members would have more time and money.

After a long discussion, a member, Mr. Ibrahim Musa, proposed that the next AGM be held on 15 December 2026. The motion was seconded by Mrs. Hauwa Bello. The Chairman asked whether all members agreed. There was no objection. The Chairman then declared that the next Annual General Meeting would be held on 15 December 2026. The annual general meeting notice sets Annual General Meeting next_meeting_date as 2026-12-15. Record status: current. This date is recorded as current in the cooperative’s minutes and will be used for all official correspondence regarding the AGM.

The Secretary was asked to send a formal notice to all members at least 21 days before the meeting. Members were also asked to suggest agenda items for the AGM in writing before the end of November.

7. Any Other Business
a. Water Pump
Mr. Samuel Eze reported that the water pump had been making a strange noise. He said that it might need a new bearing. The Chairman asked Mr. Eze to get a quotation for the repair and to present it at the next meeting.

b. Security of the Shed
Mrs. Grace Okafor reported that the lock on the shed door was weak and could be easily broken. Members agreed to buy a new padlock. The Treasurer was asked to pay for it from petty cash.

c. Harvest Festival
Mr. Danladi Yakubu suggested that the cooperative should organise a small harvest festival in August to celebrate the end of the wet season. Members agreed that this was a good idea. The Chairman said that a committee would be formed at the next meeting to plan the festival.

8. Closing
The Chairman thanked members for their attendance and contributions. The meeting ended at 12:30 p.m.

Next meeting: 8 June 2024 at 10:00 a.m.

3. Matters Arising
a. Water Pump Repairs
Mr. Samuel Eze presented the quotation he had obtained for the repair of the water pump. The quotation was from A.B. Technical Services, Karu, for the sum of NGN 18,500. The Chairman asked the Treasurer to pay the amount from the cooperative’s maintenance fund.

b. New Padlock for the Shed
Mrs. Grace Okafor reported that she had bought a new padlock for the shed door. She presented a receipt for NGN 2,800. The Treasurer was asked to reimburse her from petty cash.

c. Harvest Festival Committee
The Chairman said that a committee would be formed to plan the harvest festival. After discussion, the following members were appointed to the committee: Mrs. Hauwa Bello (Chairperson), Mr. Samuel Eze, Mr. Ibrahim Musa, and Miss Amina Sani. The committee was asked to report at the next meeting on the proposed date, venue, and budget.

4. Storage Shed Construction
The Chairman reported that the cooperative had received approval from the Karu Local Government Area for the construction of a new storage shed. The shed would be built on the plot of land behind the existing shed. The Chairman said that the cooperative had saved NGN 250,000 towards the project, but the estimated cost was NGN 620,000.

Members discussed how to raise the remaining funds. Some suggested that each member should contribute a fixed amount. Others suggested that the cooperative should apply for a loan. After a long discussion, Mr. Danladi Yakubu proposed that each of the 45 registered members should contribute NGN 5,000. This would raise NGN 225,000. The motion was seconded by Mrs. Hauwa Bello. The motion was put to a vote and was carried by a majority.

The Chairman said that the contribution would be due by 15 July 2024. Members who were unable to pay at once were asked to speak to the Treasurer to make arrangements. The Chairman also said that the cooperative would apply for a grant from the Federal Ministry of Agriculture to cover the remaining amount.

Members discussed whether to repair the tractor or to continue hiring tractors from outside. Mr. Ibrahim Musa said that hiring a tractor for ploughing cost NGN 8,000 per hectare. He said that last season the cooperative hired a tractor for 12 hectares, which cost NGN 96,000. He argued that repairing the cooperative’s own tractor would be cheaper in the long run.

GreenVale Farmers Cooperative
MEETING MINUTES – 2024 SERIES

Minutes of the 1st General Meeting of the GreenVale Farmers Cooperative Society (GVFC)
Held at the Cooperative Hall, Gwagwa Village, Kaduna State
Date: Saturday, 13 April 2024
Time: 10:00 a.m. – 1:15 p.m. (WAT)

In attendance:
1. Alhaji Musa Ibrahim – Chairman (presiding)
2. Mrs. Grace Audu – Secretary
3. Mr. Peter Danjuma – Treasurer
4. Hajiya Aisha Bello – Member
5. Mr. Samuel Okonkwo – Member
6. Mr. Tunde Adeyemi – Member
7. Mrs. Fatima Sani – Member
8. Mr. Emmanuel Nwachukwu – Member
9. Mr. John Bature – Member
10. Mrs. Maryam Abubakar – Member
11. Mr. Ibrahim Musa – Member
12. Mrs. Ruth Garba – Member

Also present: Mr. Danladi Yakubu (Field Officer, Kaduna Agricultural Development Project) as guest.

1. Opening
The Chairman welcomed all members and guests. He thanked everyone for attending the first general meeting of the year. He reminded members that the cooperative was established in 2019 and now has 47 registered members. The meeting was declared open at 10:05 a.m.

2. Reading and Adoption of the Constitution
The Chairman read out key sections of the cooperative constitution. He reminded members that the constitution is the governing document of the cooperative. According to the cooperative constitution, GreenVale Farmers Cooperative headquarters_location is Gwagwa Village, Kaduna State. Record status: current. This was noted as the official address for all correspondence and records. The Chairman called for a motion to adopt the constitution as read.

Motion: That the constitution be adopted as the governing document of the cooperative.
Proposed by: Mr. Samuel Okonkwo
Seconded by: Mrs. Fatima Sani
Vote: Unanimous

3. Report of the Treasurer
Mr. Peter Danjuma presented the financial report for the period January – March 2024.

Income:
- Members’ contributions (47 members × NGN 2,000 monthly) – NGN 282,000
- Sale of maize from last season – NGN 150,000
- Registration fees (new members) – NGN 20,000
- Total income – NGN 452,000

Expenditure:
- Purchase of fertilizer – NGN 180,000
- Fuel for tractor – NGN 45,000
- Repairs to storage shed – NGN 30,000
- Stationery and records – NGN 8,500
- Transport for produce delivery – NGN 22,000
- Total expenditure – NGN 285,500

Balance as at 31 March 2024: NGN 166,500

The Treasurer noted that the balance was lower than expected due to the cost of fertilizer. He proposed that the cooperative consider bulk purchasing of inputs to reduce costs. Members discussed this and agreed to explore the option before the next planting season.

4. Report of the Field Officer
Mr. Danladi Yakubu gave a brief talk on the upcoming farming season. He advised members to prepare their land early and to use improved seed varieties. He mentioned that the Kaduna State Government had a programme for subsidised seedlings for registered cooperatives. He asked the cooperative to submit a letter of interest to the Ministry of Agriculture before 30 April 2024.

The Chairman thanked Mr. Yakubu for his visit. He asked the Secretary to prepare the letter of interest.

5. Election of Additional Executive Members
The Chairman announced that the cooperative needed to elect two additional members to the executive committee. The positions were:
- Assistant Secretary
- Welfare Officer

Nominations were received as follows:
For Assistant Secretary:
- Mrs. Ruth Garba (nominated by Mr. John Bature, seconded by Mrs. Maryam Abubakar)
- Mr. Emmanuel Nwachukwu (nominated by Mr. Tunde Adeyemi, seconded by Hajiya Aisha Bello)

For Welfare Officer:
- Mrs. Maryam Abubakar (nominated by Mrs. Fatima Sani, seconded by Mr. Samuel Okonkwo)
- Mr. Ibrahim Musa (nominated by Mr. John Bature, seconded by Mrs. Ruth Garba)

She asked members to note that any changes to their contact details should be given to her in writing so that the list could be kept up to date.

c. Records and Filing
The Secretary reported that the cooperative's records, including minutes, financial statements, and correspondence with the Ministry, were now kept in a filing cabinet donated by the Chairman. She asked members to avoid taking files home without signing the movement register.

4. Report of the Treasurer

The Chairman thanked the Treasurer for the report.

5. Report of the Field Officer
Mr. Danladi Yakubu gave an update on the seedlings programme. He said that the cooperative's application had been received and that the Ministry would be distributing improved maize and soybean seeds to registered cooperatives in the first week of June. The cooperative had been allocated:

The Chairman asked the Secretary to prepare the documents and to liaise with the Ministry. Members agreed that the cooperative should pay the registration renewal fee of NGN 5,000.

6. Date of the Next Annual General Meeting
The Chairman raised the matter of the Annual General Meeting (AGM). He said that the cooperative’s constitution required that an AGM be held once a year. The last AGM was held in December 2023. Members discussed possible dates for the next AGM. Some members suggested holding it in October, before the harvest season. Others suggested December, after the harvest, when members would have more time and money.

After a long discussion, a member, Mr. Ibrahim Musa, proposed that the next AGM be held on 15 December 2026. The motion was seconded by Mrs. Hauwa Bello. The Chairman asked whether all members agreed. There was no objection. The Chairman then declared that the next Annual General Meeting would be held on 15 December 2026. The annual general meeting notice sets Annual General Meeting next_meeting_date as 2026-12-15. Record status: current. This date is recorded as current in the cooperative’s minutes and will be used for all official correspondence regarding the AGM.

The Secretary was asked to send a formal notice to all members at least 21 days before the meeting. Members were also asked to suggest agenda items for the AGM in writing before the end of November.

7. Any Other Business
a. Water Pump
Mr. Samuel Eze reported that the water pump had been making a strange noise. He said that it might need a new bearing. The Chairman asked Mr. Eze to get a quotation for the repair and to present it at the next meeting.

b. Security of the Shed
Mrs. Grace Okafor reported that the lock on the shed door was weak and could be easily broken. Members agreed to buy a new padlock. The Treasurer was asked to pay for it from petty cash.

c. Harvest Festival
Mr. Danladi Yakubu suggested that the cooperative should organise a small harvest festival in August to celebrate the end of the wet season. Members agreed that this was a good idea. The Chairman said that a committee would be formed at the next meeting to plan the festival.

8. Closing
The Chairman thanked members for their attendance and contributions. The meeting ended at 12:30 p.m.

Next meeting: 8 June 2024 at 10:00 a.m.

GREENVALE FARMERS COOPERATIVE
MINUTES OF THE GENERAL MEETING HELD ON 8 JUNE 2024
AT THE COOPERATIVE SHED, GWAGWA SETTLEMENT ROAD, KARU, NIGERIA

Meeting No: GV/2024/06
Time: 10:05 a.m. – 12:20 p.m.
Chairman: Alhaji Suleiman Abdullahi
Secretary: Mr. Peter Okafor

Present: 34 members (list attached to these minutes).

1. Opening
The Chairman called the meeting to order at 10:05 a.m. He welcomed members and noted that this was the first meeting after the date for the Annual General Meeting was fixed. He reminded members that the AGM would hold on 15 December 2026 as agreed at the previous meeting.

2. Reading and Adoption of Minutes of the Previous Meeting
The minutes of the meeting held on 11 May 2024 were read by the Secretary. Mr. Danladi Yakubu proposed that the minutes be adopted. The motion was seconded by Mrs. Grace Okafor. The minutes were adopted as a true record of the meeting.

3. Matters Arising
a. Water Pump Repairs
Mr. Samuel Eze presented the quotation he had obtained for the repair of the water pump. The quotation was from A.B. Technical Services, Karu, for the sum of NGN 18,500. This covered the replacement of the bearing and labour. Members asked whether the quotation was the best available. Mr. Eze said he had checked with two other workshops and this was the cheapest. The Chairman asked the Treasurer to pay the amount from the cooperative’s maintenance fund.

b. New Padlock for the Shed
Mrs. Grace Okafor reported that she had bought a new padlock for the shed door. She presented a receipt for NGN 2,800. The Treasurer was asked to reimburse her from petty cash.

c. Harvest Festival Committee
The Chairman said that a committee would be formed to plan the harvest festival. After discussion, the following members were appointed to the committee: Mrs. Hauwa Bello (Chairperson), Mr. Samuel Eze, Mr. Ibrahim Musa, and Miss Amina Sani. The committee was asked to report at the next meeting on the proposed date, venue, and budget.

4. Storage Shed Construction
The Chairman reported that the cooperative had received approval from the Karu Local Government Area for the construction of a new storage shed. The shed would be built on the plot of land behind the existing shed. The Chairman said that the cooperative had saved NGN 250,000 towards the project, but the estimated cost was NGN 620,000.

Members discussed how to raise the remaining funds. Some suggested that each member should contribute a fixed amount. Others suggested that the cooperative should apply for a loan. After a long discussion, Mr. Danladi Yakubu proposed that each of the 45 registered members should contribute NGN 5,000. This would raise NGN 225,000. The motion was seconded by Mrs. Hauwa Bello. The motion was put to a vote and was carried by a majority.

The Chairman said that the contribution would be due by 15 July 2024. Members who were unable to pay at once were asked to speak to the Treasurer to make arrangements. The Chairman also said that the cooperative would apply for a grant from the Federal Ministry of Agriculture to cover the remaining amount.

Mr. Peter Okafor suggested that the cooperative should get three quotations for the construction work. Members agreed. The Chairman appointed a building sub-committee consisting of Mr. Samuel Eze, Mr. Ibrahim Musa, and Mr. Danladi Yakubu to obtain the quotations and to present them at the next meeting.

5. Tractor Hire
Mrs. Hauwa Bello reported that the cooperative’s tractor had broken down in April and was still not working. She said that the mechanic had told her that a new gearbox was needed. The cost of the gearbox was estimated at NGN 95,000.

Members discussed whether to repair the tractor or to continue hiring tractors from outside. Mr. Ibrahim Musa said that hiring a tractor for ploughing cost NGN 8,000 per hectare. He said that last season the cooperative hired a tractor for 12 hectares, which cost NGN 96,000. He argued that repairing the cooperative’s own tractor would be cheaper in the long run.
